rationale: Hypervisor.deposit prices incoming tokens and existing reserves off the pool's instantaneous slot0 tick, so a large swap on the same pool skews the share mint and the attacker redeems a better token mix after reverting the price. The DepositProxy ratio check only bounds the deposit ratio loosely and does not use a TWAP, and no Slither finding addresses spot-price pricing.

GebProxyActions is meant to be delegatecalled from a user's DSProxy, but its functions are public with no caller check, and some SAFEs ended up owned by the library address itself. Calling quitSystem directly on the library makes the manager's ownership check pass, letting anyone move those SAFEs' collateral; the arbitrary-send-eth findings concern other functions.

A huge fCash payer leg near 2^128 produces a negative balance whose absolute value is narrowed with an unchecked uint128() cast in ExchangeRate._convertToETH, truncating the debt to zero so the free-collateral check passes. The unbacked receiver leg then settles at maturity into a real cash claim that drains the escrow; none of the reentrancy, weak-prng or uninitialized-local findings describe the cast.

Share pricing reads the vault's raw stETH balance for both the ETH share class and a separately registered stETH class, so a stETH deposit inflates the rsvETH share price without minting rsvETH. Anyone can register stETH through registerErc20; the defect code is in diamond facets that are not among the analyzed sources, and the Diamond proxy itself is not the defect.

Collateral is valued with the order-book unit price computed from fills in the current block, and the only guard is a minimum-volume gate that self-matched flash-loaned orders easily clear. The attacker pins the price at par to overvalue a cheap lend position and withdraws the TokenVault's WBTC; only forwarding-proxy sources were collected, so no finding covers the library.

The factory's order-creation entry (selector 0xbde886fc) only checks that the buyer has an active state, not that the caller is the buyer, and it accepts an attacker-chosen seller. It moves the buyer's whole account balance into an order that the seller can abort to itself; all three contracts are unverified, so names come from the trace and no source or findings exist.

Deposits mint strategy shares from the oracle-estimated value change, and FARM is valued through a thin Uniswap V3 pool with a very short TWAP window, which overprices it by about 9x. The attacker deposits FARM bought cheaply elsewhere and redeems the inflated shares for the strategy's UNI, AAVE and MKR; the controller and oracle are unverified, and the available candidates are only tokens and pairs.

solve accepts any address as the solver and pulls want tokens from it via transferFrom, so anyone holding a standing liquidETH allowance to the queue can be named solver and drained. The attacker set the amount through their own crafted request and paid victims a worthless offer token; the catalog's PoolManager address is only the cash-out venue.

ERC-404 transfer treats any value at or below maxTotalSupplyERC721 as an NFT id and moves a full unit, so when the V3 pool pays out a tiny exact-output amount it actually sends 1e18 tokens. The attacker arranged for the pool to own low ids, bought whole units for wei and sold them back for the pool's WETH; the erc721-interface findings concern function signatures, not this ambiguity.

borrow values SPIRAL collateral from the live V4 slot0 price with no TWAP or deviation cap, so a same-block pump lets borrowers draw too much ETH. The same-block guard is keyed on tx.origin, so borrowing from fresh EOAs bypasses it; Slither failed on the hook, and the PoolManager in the catalog is not the victim.
